LandingPage.faq1Answer: Not at all. The Agent Factory provides a visual, drag-and-drop interface. You describe what you want your agent to do in natural language, pick a model, attach tools — and it works. Developers can also use our REST API and Python SDK for deeper integrations.
LandingPage.faq1Question: Do I need to write code to use apowerb?
LandingPage.faq2Answer: apowerb is multi-provider by design. We support Google Gemini, OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-3.5), Anthropic Claude, Mistral, DeepSeek, and more via LiteLLM. Bring your own API keys — we never store or access your model credentials in plaintext.
LandingPage.faq3Answer: Security is foundational. All API keys are AES-encrypted at rest. Knowledge bases are isolated per organization. We support SSO via Google, Microsoft Azure, GitHub, and LinkedIn. Enterprise plans include custom guardrails, on-premise deployment, and audit logs.
LandingPage.faq4Answer: Yes! The Marketplace lets you publish agents for the community. Others can discover and clone them with one click. Cloned agents never inherit API keys — security is preserved by design.
LandingPage.faq4Question: Can I share my agents with others?
LandingPage.featureAgentFactoryDesc: Build agents visually with drag-and-drop on a React Flow canvas. 5 agent types: Base, Sequential, Parallel, Loop, Router. Undo/redo, auto-layout, and real-time execution.
LandingPage.featureAiInActionDesc: Chat with your agents in real-time. Streaming responses, code artifacts with execution, voice input, file uploads, conversation branches, and multi-session management.
LandingPage.featureBiReportingDesc: Create interactive dashboards with bar, line, and pie charts. Upload CSV data or connect to server-side queries. Auto-refresh, drag-and-drop layout, and shareable reports.
LandingPage.featureIntegrationsDesc: Connect GitHub, Google (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar), and Microsoft (Outlook). OAuth-secured tokens let agents act on external services.
LandingPage.featureKnowledgeRagDesc: Upload PDFs, CSVs, connect databases or S3 buckets. Agents search and reason over your documents with vector-powered RAG. Includes Text-to-SQL for natural language database queries.
LandingPage.featureMarketplaceDesc: Publish your agents to the community hub. Discover and clone agents with one click. Security by design — cloned agents never inherit API keys.
LandingPage.featureOrchestratorDesc: Schedule agents with cron expressions or run on-demand. Monitor execution in real-time with status tracking, logs, and the ability to cancel running jobs.
LandingPage.featureSecurityAuthDesc: Multi-factor authentication (TOTP), OAuth SSO via Google, GitHub, and Microsoft. AES-encrypted API keys, guardrails with blocked terms and tools, output schema validation.
LandingPage.featuresSubtitle: A single platform to build, run and supervise agents — from the canvas to production.
LandingPage.featureToolBoxDesc: 50+ pre-built tools — RAG search, web scraping, SQL, email, APIs. Create custom tool configurations. Organize by categories with full parameter inspection.
LandingPage.finalCtaSubtitle: Start building, orchestrating and supervising agents — in minutes, not months.
LandingPage.finalCtaTrustLine: Free to start · No credit card required
LandingPage.footerTagline: Build, orchestrate and supervise AI agents. By thaink².
LandingPage.heroSubtitle: Design, orchestrate and supervise autonomous AI agents — from idea to production in minutes. No code required.
LandingPage.heroTrustLine: Free to start · No credit card required · OAuth SSO included
LandingPage.integrationsSubtitle: Connect third-party services via OAuth. Agents read, write, and act on external platforms securely.
LandingPage.showcaseBuilderDesc: Drag agents onto a React Flow canvas. Connect them into sequential, parallel, loop, or routing flows. Configure each agent with natural language instructions, select from 10+ LLM providers, attach tools — all without writing a single line of code. Undo/redo, auto-layout, and context menus included.
LandingPage.showcaseBuilderTitle:
Design agents like
you design workflows
LandingPage.showcaseIntegrationsDesc: Connect Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs, Sheets, Calendar, GitHub, and Microsoft Outlook. Schedule agents with cron expressions — every 5 minutes, hourly, daily, or custom. Monitor every run with real-time status, logs, and cancellation.
LandingPage.showcaseIntegrationsTitle:
Agents that act
in the real world
LandingPage.showcaseRagDesc: Upload PDFs, CSVs, or connect databases and S3 buckets. Your agents automatically search, retrieve, and reason over your documents using vector-powered RAG. Includes Text-to-SQL for natural language database queries. Knowledge stays private and encrypted.

WorkflowNodeHelp.title: How to use this node
WorkflowNodeHelp.trigger_what: Starts the workflow; a workflow has exactly one. Choose below how it starts: manual (Test panel or API), webhook, schedule, email, form, file, or as a tool an agent can call.
WorkflowNodeHelp.trigger_output: the payload that started the run, as received (the Test panel JSON, the webhook body…). Read a field with '{{'{id}.field'}}'.
WorkflowNodeHelp.agent_what: Sends a message to one of your agents and waits for its reply. Leave the input field empty to send the upstream output, or write a message that inserts upstream values.
WorkflowNodeHelp.agent_output: the agent's reply: '{{'{id}'}}'. A reply that looks like JSON is read as JSON, so '{{'{id}.field'}}' works on it.
WorkflowNodeHelp.classifier_what: Asks an agent to pick one of the routes you declare, from each route's description. Link each outgoing edge to a route: only that branch runs.
WorkflowNodeHelp.classifier_output: its own input, unchanged, passed to the chosen branch. The route itself is not stored.
WorkflowNodeHelp.tool_what: Calls one tool with the arguments of the form below. Without arguments, an upstream object is passed as the arguments.
WorkflowNodeHelp.router_what: Sends the flow down one branch with rules you write, no AI. Rules are checked in order, the first match wins; otherwise the default route. Without a default route, a run that matches no rule fails.
WorkflowNodeHelp.router_output: its own input, unchanged, passed to the chosen branch. The route itself is not stored.
WorkflowNodeHelp.merge_what: Waits for every incoming edge, then continues once. Use it to join branches that all run.
WorkflowNodeHelp.merge_output: an object with one entry per incoming node: '{{'{id}.nodeId'}}' (nodeId = the id of that node).
WorkflowNodeHelp.loop_what: Repeats a body sub-workflow: for each item of a list (foreach), or until a condition is met (until). Max iterations stops it in any case.
WorkflowNodeHelp.loop_output: foreach: the list of each pass's output. until: the output of the last pass. '{{'{id}'}}'.
WorkflowNodeHelp.approval_what: Pauses the run until a person approves. Not runnable yet: validation refuses it.
WorkflowNodeHelp.try_what: Runs a body sub-workflow and retries it on error. After the last failed attempt the run does not stop: it takes the error route instead of ok.
WorkflowNodeHelp.try_output: ok: the body's output. error: '{{'{id}.code'}}', '{{'{id}.detail'}}' and '{{'{id}.node'}}' describe the failure.
WorkflowNodeHelp.subworkflow_what: Runs another of your workflows and waits for its result. Its trigger receives the input field below, or this node's input when empty.
WorkflowNodeHelp.convert_what: Changes a value's type: text, JSON, number, boolean, list, CSV or date. Leave the input field empty to convert the upstream output.
WorkflowNodeHelp.convert_output: the converted value: '{{'{id}'}}'. A failed conversion stops the run.
WorkflowNodeHelp.output_what: Sets what the workflow returns and ends the flow here: nothing can follow it. Leave Output value empty to return its input, or combine several nodes in an object.
WorkflowNodeHelp.output_output: the workflow's result, shown in the Test panel. With several Output nodes, the result gathers them by id.
WorkflowNodeHelp.http_what: Calls a public http(s) address: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, with optional headers and body.
WorkflowNodeHelp.http_output: '{{'{id}.status'}}', '{{'{id}.headers'}}' and '{{'{id}.body'}}' (JSON bodies are read as JSON).
WorkflowNodeHelp.notification_what: Sends a message: in-app notification to you, email, or Teams. Subject and message can insert upstream values.
WorkflowNodeHelp.extract_what: Asks an agent to pull the fields you declare out of a text or JSON: amounts, dates, names…
WorkflowNodeHelp.extract_output: an object with one entry per declared field; the reference to each is shown under Fields below.
WorkflowNodeHelp.rag_what: Searches an agent's knowledge base for the passages closest to the query.
WorkflowNodeHelp.rag_output: an object with the query and the passages found; the reference is shown below.
WorkflowNodeHelp.set_what: Builds an object from named fields, each a fixed value or one inserted from upstream nodes.
WorkflowNodeHelp.condition_what: Tests one or more rules (all or any must match) and takes the true or false route. Link each outgoing edge to true or false.
WorkflowNodeHelp.condition_output: its own input, unchanged, passed to the branch taken.

WorkflowTriggerGuide.title: How to use this trigger
WorkflowTriggerGuide.publishRequired: Publishing required: this trigger only listens while the workflow is published.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.publishNotRequired: No publishing needed: it runs the current saved version.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.saveFirst: Save the workflow once to get the exact call to copy.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.tokenHelp: ACCESS_TOKEN in the call is your session access token (it expires after about 2 hours). On servers with password sign-in, get one with POST /api/auth/token (form fields username and password). API keys are not accepted on this route: for an unattended caller, use a Webhook trigger instead.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.hmacHelp: Put the HMAC secret in the APOWERB_WEBHOOK_SECRET environment variable. It is shown only once, when the webhook is created or regenerated. The signature covers the exact bytes sent.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.response_sse: Response: a stream of server-sent events: node_start and node_complete for each step, route for each branch taken, then done with the final output (or error).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.response_accepted: Response: 202 with '{'"run_id": …'}' right away; the run continues in the background.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.verify_manual: Check it works: click Run in the Test panel (the sample payload is pre-filled) and follow each step. Every run, including API ones, is listed in Runs.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.verify_automatic: Check it works: first try the steps with the Test panel and the sample payload. Once published, each automatic start appears in Runs with its source.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.manual_what: Starts the workflow on demand: from the Test panel, or from another program through the API, in your name.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.manual_step1: Fill in the Sample payload above: it is what the workflow receives as '{{'{id}'}}'; read a field with '{{'{id}.field'}}'.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.manual_step2: Click Run in the Test panel: the payload is pre-filled from the sample.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.manual_step3: To start it from another program, send the call below with your access token.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.webhook_what: Starts the workflow whenever another service sends an HTTP POST to its private URL.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.webhook_step1: Optional: tick "Sign requests with an HMAC secret" so only callers holding the secret are accepted.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.webhook_step2: Publish the workflow: the webhook URL appears below, with a copy button.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.webhook_step3: Send a POST with a JSON body to that URL: the body becomes '{{'{id}'}}' (a non-object body arrives as '{{'{id}.body'}}').
WorkflowTriggerGuide.webhook_step4: If the URL leaks, click Regenerate: the old URL stops working at once.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.schedule_what: Starts the workflow on a timetable: recurring (daily, weekdays, weekly, custom cron) or once at a set time.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.schedule_step1: Choose recurring or once, then a preset or a cron expression, and the time zone.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.schedule_step2: Publish the workflow: the next run time appears below.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.schedule_step3: Each run receives '{{'{id}.scheduled_at'}}', the moment it was due.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.email_what: Starts the workflow for each new email received in your connected Outlook or Gmail inbox.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.email_step1: Connect Outlook or Gmail in Integrations (link below if it's missing).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.email_step2: Choose the provider and, if needed, filter on the sender or the subject.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.email_step4: Each matching email starts a run: '{{'{id}.from'}}', '{{'{id}.subject'}}', '{{'{id}.body'}}', '{{'{id}.to'}}', '{{'{id}.received_at'}}' and '{{'{id}.attachments'}}' (names only, never the content).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.agent_tool_what: Turns the workflow into a tool your agents can call, with typed arguments, and wait for its result.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.agent_tool_step1: Give the tool a name (lowercase, digits and _, 3 to 41 characters, unique among your workflows) and a description: the agent reads it to decide when to call the tool.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.agent_tool_step2: Declare the input fields: they become the tool's arguments, read here with '{{'{id}.field'}}'.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.agent_tool_step4: In an agent's tools, add workflow: followed by the tool name. The agent waits for the result (up to 120 s).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.form_what: Publishes a form page; each submission starts the workflow with the answers.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.form_step1: Add the fields, a title and choose who can open the form (signed-in users or anyone with the link).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.form_step2: Publish the workflow: the form link appears below, with a copy button.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.form_step3: Share the link. Each submission starts a run; the answers are '{{'{id}.field_name'}}'.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.form_step4: To invalidate a shared link, click Regenerate.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.file_what: Watches a OneDrive or Google Drive folder and starts the workflow for each new file.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.file_step1: Connect OneDrive or Google Drive in Integrations (link below if it's missing).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.file_step2: Enter the folder id, a label to recognise it, and how often to check (5 to 1440 minutes).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.file_step3: Publish the workflow: the next check time appears below.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.file_step4: Each new file starts a run: '{{'{id}.name'}}', '{{'{id}.path'}}', '{{'{id}.url'}}', '{{'{id}.size'}}', '{{'{id}.modified_at'}}' and '{{'{id}.id'}}'.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.workflow_done_what: Starts this workflow when another of your workflows finishes: to chain steps or react to failures.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.workflow_done_step1: Choose the source workflow and when to start: on success, on error, or both.
WorkflowTriggerGuide.workflow_done_step2: Publish this workflow (the source only needs to run).
WorkflowTriggerGuide.workflow_done_step3: Each start receives the source run: '{{'{id}.status'}}', '{{'{id}.output'}}', '{{'{id}.error'}}', '{{'{id}.run_id'}}' and '{{'{id}.workflow_id'}}'.
